label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Subject: Re: Saturday alarm

Kristen,

Here's the straight story. It was my popcorn.

Saturday around 10:40 I put a bag in the break room microwave, hit the popcorn button, and walked out front. A guy needed a shear pin for his snowblower, and it took longer than I figured, maybe 6 or 7 minutes. By the time I got back it was too late. We cleared the store for about 25 minutes, and the engine from up on Hertel came out. No damage, just a lot of smoke and stink.

That's on me, not the microwave. I walked away from it and I shouldn't have.

For the file, though, the September alarm wasn't me. That was the sensor in the paint aisle.

I'll cover the $175. You can take it out of my check or I'll bring cash, whichever is easier for you and Gary.

I feel bad about the customers standing out in the cold, especially the Hendersons. They've been coming in forever and I'm sure they'll be back, but that doesn't make it right that they had to walk away from a full cart.

I'd ask that you and Gary keep me on Saturdays. I like the weekend crowd and I need the hours for heating oil this winter. I can promise you this won't happen again. The no-popcorn rule is fine by me.

If it helps at all, I've been punished plenty. 31 years on the job and I get my first alarm as a civilian over a bag of butter popcorn. One of the guys on that engine was Mikey Szymanski. I broke him in as a probie back in '03, and he's never going to let me forget this. My wife said the van smelled like a burnt movie theater.

Tell Denise her coffee is coming.

Walt
